title: Saints invoked as intercessors, yet often with the same formulas used toward God
source_text: IX. Profiteri tamen Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae Sanctos invocandos esse, non ut ipsi dent bona quibus egemus, quasi eorum essent authores atque largitores, sed ut illa a Deo precibus & meritis suis nobis impetrent. Quod non obstat quominus saepe bona quaecunque corporis & animae simpliciter a Sanctis postulent, & apud Sanctos utantur iisdem precandi formulis, quibus utuntur apud Deum; etsi dicant alio sensu se illas ad Sanctos quam ad Deum dirigere.
pass_a_gloss: Yet the doctors of the Roman Church profess that the Saints are to be invoked not so that they themselves may give the goods we need, as if they were their authors and givers, but so that they may obtain those goods for us from God by their prayers and merits. That does not prevent people from often asking the Saints simply for whatever goods of body and soul, and from using toward the Saints the same formulas of prayer which they use toward God, although they say they direct those formulas to the Saints in another sense than to God.
pass_b_english: Roman doctors say Saints are asked to obtain goods from God, not to be the authors who give them.
In practice people still ask Saints outright for every bodily and spiritual good.
They use the same prayer-forms as toward God, and explain the difference as a difference of sense.

choices.why: The official claim is impetration, not authorship of grace.
rejected: that they may only be remembered
